summary: Three protect. Three connect. Two work together.
sourceLabel: Working editorial draft, unreviewed coaching guidance
idea: Three protect. Three connect. Two work together.
playerFacing: Our back three give us cover. Our midfield three link both ends. Our two forwards give us somewhere to play and press together. We move as the ball moves.

ruleTable.title: Middle first
ruleTable.say: Protect the route to our goal before chasing wide.
ruleTable.question: Press or cover?

ruleTable.title: Ball side wide, far side in
ruleTable.say: Give width near the ball; the far midfielder comes inside to help.
ruleTable.question: Stay wide or tuck in?

ruleTable.title: One comes, one goes
ruleTable.say: Our two forwards shouldn't make the same run.
ruleTable.question: Offer feet or threaten behind?

ruleTable.title: Go together, recover together
ruleTable.say: If one presses, others close the next pass; if beaten, recover as a unit.
ruleTable.question: Are teammates close enough to help?

considerations.label: Coaching judgement in the draft, not reviewed
tradeoffs: wide midfielders have significant two-way responsibility
an isolated central midfielder can be overloaded
two strikers can be disconnected when midfield sits too deep
pressing with just two forwards may leave an easy central pass

reviewQuestions: Is the selected midfield shape a flat 3 or should 8 sometimes be deeper? What is the simplest way to teach that without rigidity?
Against a team with two central midfielders or three high attackers, how do we keep useful cover?
When an outside defender goes, who must remain? Is a rule similar to the original One goes, one stays appropriate?
Are the four names understandable and actionable for U12 to U13 players?
Are there situations in which far-side midfield should stay wide rather than tuck in?
Does the proposed two-striker press risk leaving the centre open? What is the safest child-friendly correction?
Do sessions promote learning, role rotation and enjoyment rather than rigid compliance?
Confirm offside illustrations, set-piece guidance, and competition-rule statements before publication.

rules.title: Middle first
rules.tag: Protect the route to our goal before chasing wide.
rules.summary: Protect the middle before committing more than one player to the ball.
rules.extra: If somebody steps towards the ball, somebody else needs to protect the central route.
look: Watch whether pressure on the ball has cover behind it.
Check whether 8 remains connected to the back three.
Decide who can press rather than sending everybody towards the same player.

rules.title: Ball side wide, far side in
rules.tag: Give width near the ball; the far midfielder comes inside to help.
rules.summary: Support the player in possession without crowding their space.
rules.extra: If a switch of play is on, the far player may need to remain wider.
rules.seo: Ball side wide, far side in: 9v9 3-3-2 playing principle
look: Is 7 or 11 offering a useful wide pass?
Can 8 connect play without becoming isolated?
Does the far midfielder need to come inside, or stay available for a switch?

rules.title: One comes, one goes
rules.tag: Our two forwards shouldn't make the same run.
rules.summary: One forward can offer a pass to feet while the other threatens space.
rules.extra: These roles can reverse. Any run beyond opponents must be timed to stay onside.
rules.seo: One comes, one goes: 9v9 3-3-2 playing principle
look: Are 9 and 10 offering different passing options?
Is 8 close enough to combine with the forwards?
Can a forward recognise when there is no useful space to run into?

rules.title: Go together, recover together
rules.tag: If one presses, others close the next pass; if beaten, recover as a unit.
rules.summary: Pressing depends on help from nearby teammates, not one player chasing alone.
rules.cue: Are teammates close enough to help?
rules.extra: The first defender delays; others must decide which spaces and passing options to protect.
rules.seo: Go together, recover together: 9v9 3-3-2 playing principle
look: Does the first presser have help behind and alongside?
Can the other forward restrict the easy central pass?
After pressure is beaten, does the team recover into useful positions?

issue.intro: Three protect. Three connect. Two work together. A 9v9 starting picture with three defenders, three midfielders and two forwards who must offer different options.
issue.summary: A proposed 3-3-2 starting shape, four playing principles, positional responsibilities and how the team works together.

roles.title: Goalkeeper
roles.head: Start, see, speak
points: Start by looking for a simple pass to a teammate who can receive.
Keep talking to the back three about opponents and space.
Before choosing a pass, think about what happens if we lose it.
roles.cue: Who is free, and what happens if I pass there?

roles.title: Centre-back
roles.head: See the whole picture
points: Help organise the three defenders and recognise danger through the centre.
When stepping towards an opponent, know which teammate can provide cover.
Connect with 8 when there is a sensible passing option.
roles.cue: If I step in, who's behind me?

roles.title: Outside defenders
roles.head: Defend, support, cover
points: Recognise when to challenge a wide opponent and when to protect the centre.
Support teammates in possession without both leaving the defence exposed.
Work with 5 and the nearby midfielder to share pressure and cover.

roles.title: Central midfielder
roles.head: Connect both ends
points: Give teammates a useful central passing option when we have the ball.
Notice when moving towards the ball would leave an open route through midfield.
Keep connected to both the back three and two forwards.
roles.cue: Can they play through us if I move?

roles.title: Wide midfielders
roles.head: Width and hard work
points: Offer width when your team needs an outside passing option.
When the ball is on the far side, consider whether coming inside would help your team.
Recover to support the defence when possession changes.
roles.cue: Should I be wide or inside right now?

roles.title: Two forwards
roles.head: Partners, not passengers
points: Offer different options: one may come short while the other stays higher.
Recognise when you can pressure the ball and when your partner needs help.
Stay connected to the midfield instead of waiting together for a long pass.

gives: a three-player midfield linking both ends
a partner for each of our two forwards
opportunities to use width and combinations
